To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce the concept and implementation of crash-resistance for client-side applications.
client-side applications can be exploited in a way that they can be crashed and restarted to scan memory or execute code-reuse attacks, which is a novel concept.

we developed a crash-resistance method that enables memory scanning of client applications, which is the first method that can be applied to client software, and furthermore that we show the advantages of our crash-resistance primitive to defeat code-reuse defense mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: (i) we show that client applications can be crash-resistant, (ii) we develop a novel memory scanner based on memory oracles without control-flow hijacking, and (iii) we show how crash-resistance weaks defenses against code-reuse and diversification.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
client applications can be crash-resilient and that this property can be used to circumvent certain defensive mechanisms against code-reuse.
crash-resistance is a serious threat to current security models and needs to be addressed by new defensive schemes in the near future.
crash-resistance is an underestimated threat to the security of the Internet and needs immediate attention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce the concept that client applications can be crash-resistant and thus are able to survive memory corruption attacks, even if they are not designed to do so.
client-side crash-resistance is a severe problem that needs to be addressed in order to achieve a more secure system.
crash-resistance is a powerful primitive that needs to be taken into account for defensive code randomization schemes and that the concept of oracles is a valuable tool for future research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security of a system is only as strong as the weakest link, and that a single vulnerability can be used to compromise a whole system, even in the presence of counter-measures.
the security of a program is not only dependent on the security of its own code but also on the security of other programs.
crash-resistant applications can be used to overcome diversification and information hiding, and that this is not only limited to network services.
